Using design_type "presentation" with length "comprehensive" reliably produces 15+ slides but AI-generated layouts pack too much text per slide for content-heavy curriculum catalogs, making it unsuitable for dense multi-bullet outlines. The Canva doc type with verbatim set to True preserves exact markdown copy without AI rewriting, making it preferable when content fidelity matters more than visual polish. For high-fidelity print output, building HTML with wkhtmltopdf using explicit flags --page-width 8.5in --page-height 11in -B 0 -L 0 -R 0 -T 0 produces exact US Letter dimensions; relying on CSS @page alone defaults to A4. TeX Gyre Heros is available in the environment and serves as a reliable Helvetica substitute for clean sans-serif print design.

Claude pivoted to building a single consolidated export file at /home/claude/brett-memory-export.md, reading all 73 files across /profile.md, /preferences.md, /topics/ (6 files), /people/ (12 files), and /areas/ (53 files) and appending them sequentially with exact frontmatter and full contents preserved. The work completed 64 of 73 files before the response reached its limit, with the 9 largest /areas/ files (can-enterprise, catalytic-sundays, family-legacy-by-design, family-legacy-intelligence, generosity-ministry, living-obedience, macro-edition, master-title-directory, staff-intelligence) remaining to be appended in a follow-up. Claude informed Brett of this clearly and requested he say "continue" to finish. **Tool knowledge** Claude used memory_list (with include_preview: true) to retrieve the full 73-file directory with paths and descriptions grouped by folder, then used memory_read with array-style multi-path parameters to batch-read files efficiently — pulling up to 12 paths in a single call rather than one at a time. For the consolidated file build, Claude used create_file to initialize the export document with the first block of content, then used bash_tool with heredoc syntax (cat >> /path/file <<'DELIMITER' ... DELIMITER) to append subsequent content blocks without overwriting prior content. After each append operation, wc -c was run on the file to confirm cumulative byte count and verify the file was growing correctly. The heredoc delimiter MEMX_EOF_9 was used consistently across all append operations to avoid conflicts with the markdown content being written. The reliable pattern for this type of multi-block file build is: create_file for the first block, then bash_tool heredoc appends for all subsequent blocks, with a byte-count check after each to confirm integrity.
